subject: Post-demo: evaluation plan, model shortlist, and streaming UX follow-ups
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@finserve.ai>, Priya Rao <priya@finserve.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2026 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: evaluation plan, model shortlist, and streaming UX follow-ups

Thanks again for taking the demo today — great conversation. This thread is a concise recap + proposed evaluation plan so we can get a pilot kicked off quickly. I pulled together the items we discussed and highlighted the streaming UX issues you flagged.

Quick recap of requirements you emphasized:
- Low-latency streaming for live agent assist (target steady-state per-token latency <= 150ms)
- Strong stop-sequence reliability for structured responses (internal marker: ‘### END’)
- Preserve partial-output coherence (avoid one-line mid-sentence repeats when streaming)
- Cost sensitivity: prefer a model under $X/token for production; pilot budget ~100k tokens
- Compliance: SOC 2 and restricted data handling required

Recommended model shortlist to evaluate (two-tier approach):
1) rw-7b-v1 (optimized quantized profile) — baseline for cost/latency trade-offs
2) rw-13b-optim (better instruction-following; candidate for higher-quality outputs)
3) rw-30b-quant-lite (if we hit quality ceiling on rw-13b)

Why these: rw-7b gives the best price-performance for streaming with prefix caching; rw-13b improves structured outputs (stop sequences) in our pre-evals. rw-30b is a fallback if we see regression on long-form coherence during the pilot.

Pre-eval notes (from our internal runs):
- Stop-sequence mismatch: with streaming enabled, ‘### END’ failed to trigger ~6% of the time on a 2000-sample prompt set (attached streaming_test_vectors.csv).
- Partial-output mid-sentence repetition: observed when token window expands beyond 512 tokens; we believe KV-cache alignment in streaming path needs tuning.
- Latency: median token latency ~120ms, p95 ~780ms on long contexts during burst traffic (non-production cluster).

Attachments included here: finserve_prompt_set_v1.txt (prioritized prompts + edge cases), streaming_test_vectors.csv (vectorized tests we ran), pilot_scope_estimate.pdf (cost/time SOW stub).

Proposed next steps and timeline:
1) Confirm pilot scope and success criteria (you to confirm acceptance thresholds for stop-sequence reliability and p95 latency).
2) Redwood runs A/B: rw-7b-v1 (quantized) vs rw-13b-optim with identical prompt set + streaming enabled — 2 weeks for tuning/prompt engineering.
3) Pilot period: 2-week live pilot with up to 100k tokens (we handle instrumentation + eval harness).
4) Post-pilot review: quality metrics, latency, and cost analysis; recommend production model & deployment profile.

Questions for you:
- Can you confirm the procurement contact and whether a PO will be required to start the pilot?
- Any additional acceptance thresholds (e.g., maximum allowed stop-sequence failure rate)?
- Preferred kickoff window — we can start as early as July 20th.

Links: evaluation report template: https://drive.redwood.internal/finserve/evals/rw-eval-report-20260713.pdf
HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.com/deal/FS-2026-07-13

Thanks — I attached the prompt set and test vectors: finserve_prompt_set_v1.txt, streaming_test_vectors.csv.

—
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0132

From: Samir Patel <samir@finserve.ai>

Subject: Re: Post-demo: evaluation plan, model shortlist, and streaming UX follow-ups

Vanessa — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifying items from our side:  
1) Priority for us is stop-sequence reliability and consistent partial-output coherence — if the model frequently fails to stop on ‘### END’ that will block live deployment. What do you recommend as an acceptance threshold? We were thinking <=2% failure.  
2) Can you prioritize the prompt set so we get the corner cases first?  
3) Procurement: I’ll loop in our finance lead but a PO will likely be required; can you share a high-level cost estimate for the 2-week pilot (token and infra estimate)?  

Also — SOC 2 compliance is required; do you have the SOC 2 report and an SOC 2 AICPA letter we can review?

If we can get the prioritized prompts and an estimated pilot cost today, we can route to Finance and potentially start next week.

Thanks,
Samir
Director of Product 
FinServe AI

- Stop-sequence success >= 98% on the prioritized prompt set
- Partial-output coherence: no mid-sentence repetition >3% on live agent scenarios
- Latency: median token latency < 150ms, p95 < 500ms under pilot traffic

Pilot cost estimate (rough):
- Baseline rw-7b-v1 pilot (2 weeks, 100k tokens): estimated $1,200 + infra (observability/retention): $600 — total ~ $1,800
- rw-13b-optim pilot (same scope): estimated $2,800 + infra $600 — total ~ $3,400
